(Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! (Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase!
