(Achievement of the Year) ] || ---------------- || (This is a review of installing a dishwasher and remodeling the sink.) When I moved into a new apartment, I did some interior design and bought appliances and furniture, and the first thing I considered was a dishwasher! I saw a commercial dishwasher while working part-time at a cafe and was blown away by its new design. However, I couldn't afford a commercial dishwasher at home, and due to budget constraints during the move, I looked for branded, reasonably priced products. Korea's leading home appliance brands are Samsung and L*ny, and Samsung products are more affordable, so I ended up choosing almost all Samsung products. There's a saying that "L*" is a household name for appliances, so when I moved to my parents' house, I had all the Samsung products, but this time, my budget didn't allow it. I had been very satisfied with the built-in Samsung appliances in my previous studio apartment, so I trusted them and bought a Samsung product. The installation process: I'd been eyeing the dishwasher on Coupang for a few days, and when the price improved, I bought it. I scheduled the installation for the day I moved in. The day before the installation, I got a call to schedule a visit. The dishwasher was unusual in that the sink remodeler came first, and then the dishwasher installer came separately. The remodeling felt like a bigger and more important task than the dishwasher installation, and it actually took longer. I wasn't very busy moving, but the installer came and went, and I think it took about an hour. They had to make room for the dishwasher, so in our case, we removed the oven under the induction range and installed the dishwasher there. However, the countertop didn't match, so we had to pay for the remodeling. ((It came out to be in the mid-100,000 won range, so I paid for it separately from the dishwasher.)) I didn't realize there was an additional remodeling fee, and it was even in the 100,000 won range. But I paid for the dishwasher anyway. The remodeling was incredibly thorough. They even applied film to the kitchen sink a week before the move, and they said it was a good idea to apply the film after the dishwasher was installed. Our house was installed in the following order: sink film removal, move-in cleaning, and dishwasher installation. The installer said it's better to install the dishwasher first because the film could peel off or cause problems during installation. 1. The best appliance in my life: a dishwasher. I used to get so angry when I came home that the sink was full of dishes to wash, and I'd get so angry when I had to wash them and cook. But now, even when the sink is full of dishes, I don't complain at all. It still feels like play. I don't feel the burden of washing dishes anymore. As I got older, my shoulders would hurt from washing dishes, and my back would get sore from standing for long periods. I'd often take breaks and then start again. But since the dishwasher arrived, dishwashing stress has disappeared. 2. A dishwasher with a maximum capacity of 14 people. People always say you should buy a 14-person dishwasher, but I think bigger is always better. I'm thinking about getting another 14-person dishwasher. It seats 14 people, but if you add a rice cooker inner pot, wok, or frying pan, the lower compartment is almost full. I think it was a good decision to get a large capacity. I'm still new to using it, so it was a bit difficult to stack dishes neatly. 3. Easy operation. I've never seen a home dishwasher before, and I saw it for the first time during installation. The technician showed me how to do it, but I forgot about it the next time I left, so I tried again and it was easy. 4. Cleanliness. I use Pro* dishwasher detergent, which is the most commonly used, and at first, there was some detergent residue, but with use, that residue disappeared and now it's clean. I used to use one bottle of Pro* dishwasher detergent, but I cut it in half. This half-bottle size is just the right amount, and the dishes feel cleaner. Sometimes, water collects where I place dishes upside down, and that water seems to contain detergent residue. Sometimes, I rinse the dishes with water to check if I washed them properly. I also pre-wash the dishes. There are still a few things to do with the dishwasher, rather than just throwing them in, but I'm so glad I bought it. Washing dishes takes a lot of effort and time, like scrubbing them with a sponge and then rinsing them thoroughly with water. But with the dishwasher, I've saved time, labor, and the mental stress associated with washing dishes. Stress is the root of all evil. Mental health is paramount, and this dishwasher makes me feel like I'm taking care of my mental health. I didn't research dishwashers well and bought them because of the brand and price, but foreign brands cost millions of won. This is the best domestic brand, and with this performance at this price, I think I made a good purchase! Sentence (English): We purchased this dishwasher from Costco in July 2024, and Costco subcontracted the installation to Pacific West.
Comments (English): [ Serious Water Damage Caused by Costco Sub - PW ] || ---------------- || We purchased this dishwasher from Costco in July 2024, and Costco subcontracted the installation to Pacific West. Unfortunately, this decision turned into a long-term nightmare.During installation, the Pacific West technician pressured and scammed my tenant into paying $100 for a plastic air gap and also insisted on installing a new dedicated electrical outlet, claiming it was required. My tenant trusted the installer and paid.According to my tenant, the technician worked under the sink for 20–30 minutes, mentioned that he “ran into some difficulties,” but said everything was eventually resolved.The real nightmare surfaced over a year later.My tenant noticed water leaking inside the kitchen cabinets and onto the floor. By the time it was discovered, the kitchen cabinet was already severely rotted, and the wood flooring had buckled from prolonged moisture exposure.Initially, we suspected the dishwasher itself and contacted Costco. Costco sent out a Whirlpool technician confirmed there was only minor leakage at the front, which could not explain the extensive damage. Whirlpool refused to investigate further.We then hired our own plumber, who discovered the shocking truth:When the Pacific West technician installed the new outlet, he carelessly drilled through the back panel of the sink cabinet and drilled THREE holes directly into the drain pipe behind it. This caused the drain pipe—hidden behind the cabinet—to leak slowly for over a year, leading to mold, rotted cabinets, damaged flooring, and ruined baseboards.When we filed a claim with Costco, they sent Pacific West to inspect their own work. • The first technician admitted that the drain pipe leak was related to their installation error. • Later, a second technician was sent, who completely changed the story and denied responsibility, claiming the holes were “not made by them,” and used every excuse possible to avoid liability.We do have video evidence showing the original technician stating he would install the outlet and replace the air gap. Unfortunately, we did not record the drilling process itself. Despite this, the evidence is extremely clear: • This kitchen never leaked before the dishwasher installation • The three holes in the drain pipe align exactly with the three screws used for the newly installed outlet by Pacific WestIsn't that evidence enough? Sadly, Costco's claims department has been extremely disappointing. Instead of standing up for their customer, they repeatedly asked us to provide “more proof,” while ignoring the obvious facts. The dishwasher was installed in July 2024 and the water damage was discovered in Nov. 2025. This issue has now dragged on for over three months with no resolution.After this experience—and after later reading numerous Yelp reviews reporting the same $100 air-gap scam and unprofessional behavior—I strongly advise: If you have a choice, DO NOT allow Pacific West to install your dishwasher.Their technicians are unprofessional, careless, and their mistakes can cause serious, hidden damage that only appears long after they leave.This has been an exhausting, costly, and completely avoidable ordeal.

Sentence (English): In 47 years of marriage, I have never owned a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Love my dishwasher ] || ---------------- || In 47 years of marriage, I have never owned a dishwasher. I was thrilled when my husband agreed it was finally time to get one. After talking to a lot of people who have dishwashers, many agreed that a Bosch was the most reliable and worth the higher cost. We've had our Bosch for over a month. My husband installed it and the next day we put in our dirty dishes and were so happy with how clean they were. It's definitely quiet. We can hardly tell it's running. There's a little red light you can see on the floor to tell it is running. We have it blue toothed to my phone and I get a kick out of the announcement on my phone when the dishwasher has completed its cycle. I can even change the settings on my phone. I did this as I wanted the door to automatically open when the cycle completed to aid in drying. That's an added feature we thought was pretty cool. I also like that I don't have to wash the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher. We just scrape off excess food and load. They come out clean everytime. I need to become better at loading. Still haven't become great at that, but I'll get there. Anyway, couldn't be happier with the dishwasher. My dishpan hands are grateful, too!

Sentence (English): My first Bosch dishwasher lasted 21 years.
Comments (English): [ 2nd Bosch - Very good but not as great as 1st ] || ---------------- || My first Bosch dishwasher lasted 21 years. It had no issues, was very quiet, cleaned dishes well, and I loved it! When it suddenly stopped working, I didn't do any research - I already knew I wanted another Bosch. I went to my favorite appliance store, quickly reviewed features on the 2 options in my price range, and bought it. Quick and easy! Once it was installed in my kitchen I began to notice differences compared to my first one. 1. It's still very quiet and I love that! 2. It seems to run much longer than the previous one. Some options run over 2 hours. That's crazy! 3. This model projects a red light in the floor while running. My kitchen island means I can't see the light from many angles. Plus, it doesn't project a green (or other) light when it's done. This means I don't always remember later that I ran the dishwasher and need to empty it. 4. It has a feature to pop the door open to cool when it's done. Otherwise, condensation builds inside the machine. This is a major design flaw and I likely would have done more research on other models or brands if I knew this. Who in the world wants hot, humid air released into their kitchen? I live in Florida! The answer is never! Plus, I have older laminate countertops. This would damage my countertop if I used that option. 5. The racks feel cheaper, less substantial, and the center hand pulls are poorly placed. On my old unit I could easily grab the corner of the rack and slide it out. Everyone stands to the side of an open dishwasher to load/unload it. The center pull is inconvenient causing me to reach or lean further to grab it. 6. My model has some tines that will lay down if needed. They're located right next to immovable tines, so I've yet to notice a difference in having them up or down. Additionally, some of them won't stay up. 7. The top silverware rack is less impressive than expected. I was initially very excited about this new feature. The rack feels flimsy. I can lay perhaps 6 large serving spoons up there and the space is essentially full. It's alright but not a game changer of any kind. 8. I feel like I can't get as many dishes in the dishwasher as my previous model. That doesn't seem like it would be true but even my husband, who doesn't regularly load the dishwasher, noticed it. The top (middle if you have the silverware rack) rack doesn't seem to hold bowls quite right, almost like they're sized for non-standard size bowls. And if have the silverware rack, you have very little wiggle room for any item to be slightly raised. 9. Dishes come out very clean so I'm happy with that feature. 10. The top/middle rack has a tilt feature that allows water to run off area it sometimes stays pooled, such as the bottom rim of an upside down coffee cup. I'm still a big Bosch fan based on my experience with my first one. I'm reserving judgment on this 500 series I purchased and hope it continues to do all the things it does well for another 20 years. But I also hope they take this review into consideration because it needs some adjustments.

Sentence (English): We bought this together with a KitchenAid refrigerator to finish our kitchen remodel.
Comments (English): [ Irreparable Leaks ] || ---------------- || We bought this together with a KitchenAid refrigerator to finish our kitchen remodel. A rather expensive combination. The dishwasher started leaking in December 2025. We hired the appliance repair person that we've used for years to help us. He determined that the sump assembly was leaking and charged us $110 for the diagnostic service and we were told that the new sump assembly and labor would be an additional $400. We contacted Costco for warranty assistance, were told that the manufacturer warranty had recently expired a few months earlier and that we needed contact Citibank for a claim on the "Included" extended warranty. Many hurdles were placed in the way to resolution. To the point of frustration that we gave up and decided to deal with it ourselves. The part was ordered, Gregg came out today, installed the brand new sump pump assembly and it STILL leaks! There is a design flaw with this machine, and I'm sure we aren't the only ones dealing with it. The bottom of the stainless steel tub does NOT seal properly with the pump assembly gasket. The repair tech provided us with some direct contact phone numbers to Whirlpool, who actually make the KitchenAid products, in hopes that they would assist us with some resolution. He noted there is also water damage to our floor. We paid him the $377 charge for parts and labor putting us at a grand total of approximately half the cost of a brand new machine and away he went leaving us with a non-resolved, and quite expensive, parts and labor bill for a dishwasher that still does NOT work.Stay away from this machine and quite frankly anything with the KitchenAid label and beware of the "Included" extended warranty offering. It's absolutely worthless. Nothing but a marketing ploy to give Costco members a false sense of security.

Things I liked:- That the door auto-opens at the end of the cycle to allow the steam to escape. However, I do not like that it opens before it is actually finished drying such that the door is open while the cycle "finishes" (often for over 60 minutes), so the dishes don't actually get properly dried, they come out much wetter than previous dishwashers - The tines are angled to make it easier to stack dishes- I like the idea of the "auto sense" option to detect when the dishes are clean to end the cycle rather than continuing unneccesarily, however it doesn't seem to actually work very well as dishes are often left with stuck on food residue - That the top rack height can be adjusted to allow tall glasses to fitThings I didn't like/ need improvement:- The control buttons are on the top of the door and they covered by the counter when the door is closed so you cannot press the buttons or see how much time is left when the door is closed- There is no easily accessible option to turn of the door "auto open" function (see above)- Top rack layout of the tines: there are two shallow "rows" without tines in the middle, and these are useless to actually put anything in, cups don't sit properly, you can't put plastic containers because they flip over and get filled with water (you can't really put small plastic containers anywhere in the top rack as they flip over and get filled with water everywhere), and the remaining "rows" are mostly to narrow to comfortably put cups anywhere- Bottom rack layout is mostly ok and you can fit quite a few dishes, but the cutlery rack just sits in the bottom rack instead of clipping in anywhere so it isn't the best use of space - The dishes just don't get cleaned as well as my old (really old) dishwasher, there is often residual stuck-on food on several plates and pieces of cutlery, regardless of amount of dishwashing detergent used, and regardless of letting the sink water run hot before starting the dishwasher- Dishes don't get dried properly, and anything light gets flipped over and filled with water- There is no "express" or quick cycle

Comments (English): [ Very impressed with this 300 series dishwasher ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) After approximately one month of ownership and running the dishwasher daily, I must say that I am truly impressed. It seems to be really high-build quality. I like everything about it. Buttons do not feel 100% durable, but time will tell. You can use an app to start or schedule the programs. I use "Auto" cycle daily, and sometimes "Normal". Very clean and very dry. I think it's important to use a rinsing agent (actually a drying agent ) because dishes come out dry every time. I do not use salt, and I use a quality detergent. Racks are adjustable, and the third rack is a must. You'll get better over time at organizing dishes in the racks, but I would not change a thing for my needs. My previous dishwasher lasted 22 years withour service call and it was from another brand. I'll keep my fingers crossed that this dishwasher has a long life ahead without giving me any trouble. Highly recommended.

Sentence (English): We needed to get a new dishwasher and my husband wanted to spend more to get a better quality dishwasher, so we got this one and I don't think I've ever hated an appliance more.
Comments (English): [ Waste of money for us ] || ---------------- || We needed to get a new dishwasher and my husband wanted to spend more to get a better quality dishwasher, so we got this one and I don't think I've ever hated an appliance more. It cleans pretty well, but not any better than our old dishwasher, so I'm unimpressed there, but worse, it's terrible at drying. We usually use the disinfect setting and often use the auto-open function, but in both cases, the dishes come out much wetter than any of our previous dishwashers did and even the dishes that are relatively dry feel slightly damp. There's almost always a steamy feeling inside of it even if it's cool. The auto-open function might help better if it opened sooner and to a lesser degree so that steam could rush out and dry the dishes. Maybe they don't do it that way because it could be a safety issue, but if it plays a warning sound and flash a light before opening, I think it would be fine. The controls are also difficult to deal with at times. You can't tell where to press to make selections or if there are even options to select and sometimes, the buttons you know are there. somewhere. don't work. I also hate the placement. I am constantly hitting buttons by accident when the door is open. Maybe that's just me. I know I wouldn't have that problem if I just kept the door closed, but it's usually open because we're trying to let the dishes dry more. The only good things I can say about this thing are that it's very quiet (but so was our last one), it looks nice (but I really don't care), and it apparently has a feature that alerts us if there's a leak, which is a nice feature, but untested and hopefully will never need to be tested. I'd be as annoyed with a cheaper dishwasher if it left dishes as wet as this one does, but this one is especially upsetting since it cost a lot more than one we could have been happier with. This got so many good reviews. Maybe we got a faulty one.

Sentence (English): I got the chance to try the Bosch 300 Series 24-inch Front Control Built-in Dishwasher right when I was seriously over my old, loud, not-so-great-at-cleaning machine.
Comments (English): [ Cleans great, wish it held more ] || ---------------- || I got the chance to try the Bosch 300 Series 24-inch Front Control Built-in Dishwasher right when I was seriously over my old, loud, not-so-great-at-cleaning machine. With a big family and dishes piling up constantly, I needed something that could actually keep up and not sound like a jet taking off in the kitchen.First thing I noticed? This thing is super quiet. Like, “Is it even on? ” quiet. I can run it during dinner, while we're watching TV, or late at night, and it never interrupts anything. That alone makes it feel like a huge upgrade. It also looks beautiful. The clean front design and sleek finish give the kitchen a more modern, polished look without trying too hard.Most importantly, it gets dishes really clean. I'm talking dried-on food, greasy pans, cloudy glasses — all coming out spotless. I've been able to stop pre-rinsing so much, which saves time and honestly just makes life easier. That's a big deal when you're running loads every single day.I also love the smart features. The remote control and notifications through the app are fantastic. I can check the status from my phone and get an alert when the cycle's done. It's one of those features you don't think you need — until you have it.That said, there is one thing I wish I'd known ahead of time: the interior feels smaller than my previous dishwasher. It's well designed, and the racks move smoothly, but it just doesn't hold as much. For our family of seven, we're running and unloading it multiple times a day. If you've got a big household, that's definitely something to think about.Overall though, I'm really impressed. It's quiet, stylish, well-built, and does an excellent job cleaning. I'd say it's perfect for small to medium families or anyone who wants powerful performance plus modern, connected features.

Sentence (English): I bought this unit because we have a house that had all GE Appliances.
Comments (English): [ Help! MY Beautiful GE Blk Stainless Dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || I bought this unit because we have a house that had all GE Appliances. We needed to upgrade our Appliances. New GE Fridge Blk Stainless, great product for 5 yrs. New GE gas 5 burner range, works great because of GE design and engineering, beautiful. We bought a new GE dishwasher, beautiful Blk Stainless, but it doesn't work very well, It can't complete a wash cycle. I have tried repair service, which was Sears, contracted through Asurion Ins. That didn't go well. I didn't use it for a year, then I tried and it decided to start washing again, but not going through a complete wash cycle. I messed around with the control console trying various combinations of "press and release" multiple switches and stumbled upon a code"371", which was a system LED check. The control console seemed to work flawlessly. All LEDs lit up perfectly. I hope I eliminated the control console as a suspect to the operation of the Dishwasher. I stumbled upon another "Push and Release" for 1- 8 diagnostic test cycles for probably all of the mechanical functions; 1 - drains the washer., 3 & 4 - go through a 2- minute wash cycle.There are so many wash cycle combinations that I can't stand there to diagnose each wash cycle. I have stayed with just one wash/rinse and dry cycle. This is the "normal wash cycle (80 min.) wash , rinse, & dry cycle - w/ the Wash Temp Boost" feature which extends the wash, rinse, & dry cycle to (111 min.) This is the 2nd PCB for the complete dishwasher operations that is in my dishwasher. I know software has to be loaded into the PCB's processor. I don't know the version software that was on this replaced PCB, but I do know that it can't be the correct version to make it finish a complete wash, rinse, & dry cycle. If GE monitors this "Product Review" site, I would greatly appreciate the most updated PCB with the latest firmware update so my beautiful Blk Stainless Dishwasher can finish a wash cycle and stay in my home. I don't want to have to switch the GE Blk Stainless Dishwasher out with a similar LG or Samsung model. I love the stainless interior, the 3 racks are well designed, & very, very quiet. You almost need a stethoscope to listen to the various cycles operate. I will change my review if GE can come up with the correct fix to this beautiful GE Blk Stainless Dishwasher. M Medley

Sentence (English): I bought this unit because we have a house that had all GE Appliances.
Comments (English): [ Help! MY Beautiful GE Blk Stainless Dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || I bought this unit because we have a house that had all GE Appliances. We needed to upgrade our Appliances. New GE Fridge Blk Stainless, great product for 5 yrs. New GE gas 5 burner range, works great because of GE design and engineering, beautiful. We bought a new GE dishwasher, beautiful Blk Stainless, but it doesn't work very well, It can't complete a wash cycle. I have tried repair service, which was Sears, contracted through Asurion Ins. That didn't go well. I didn't use it for a year, then I tried and it decided to start washing again, but not going through a complete wash cycle. I messed around with the control console trying various combinations of "press and release" multiple switches and stumbled upon a code"371", which was a system LED check. The control console seemed to work flawlessly. All LEDs lit up perfectly. I hope I eliminated the control console as a suspect to the operation of the Dishwasher. I stumbled upon another "Push and Release" for 1- 8 diagnostic test cycles for probably all of the mechanical functions; 1 - drains the washer., 3 & 4 - go through a 2- minute wash cycle.There are so many wash cycle combinations that I can't stand there to diagnose each wash cycle. I have stayed with just one wash/rinse and dry cycle. This is the "normal wash cycle (80 min.) wash , rinse, & dry cycle - w/ the Wash Temp Boost" feature which extends the wash, rinse, & dry cycle to (111 min.) This is the 2nd PCB for the complete dishwasher operations that is in my dishwasher. I know software has to be loaded into the PCB's processor. I don't know the version software that was on this replaced PCB, but I do know that it can't be the correct version to make it finish a complete wash, rinse, & dry cycle. If GE monitors this "Product Review" site, I would greatly appreciate the most updated PCB with the latest firmware update so my beautiful □□ Blk Stainless Dishwasher can finish a wash cycle and stay in my home. I don't want to have to switch the GE Blk Stainless Dishwasher out with a similar LG or Samsung model. I love the stainless interior, the 3 racks are well designed, & very, very quiet. You almost need a stethoscope to listen to the various cycles operate. I will change my review if GE can come up with the correct fix to this beautiful □□ GE Blk Stainless Dishwasher. M Medley

Sentence (English): We chose the Bosch SHP65CM5N because it felt like the best of both worlds: it fit within our budget while still offering many of the features we wanted in a modern dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Quiet, Powerful, worth the Investment ] || ---------------- || We chose the Bosch SHP65CM5N because it felt like the best of both worlds: it fit within our budget while still offering many of the features we wanted in a modern dishwasher. After several months of use, we'd rate it a solid 9 out of 10. I would absolutely buy it again and would confidently recommend it to others. Cleaning Performance This dishwasher just works. Heavily soiled dishes and pans consistently come out sparkling clean on the first wash. We've had very few issues overall. The only minor exception is that occasionally heavily soiled utensils placed on the top rack don't get completely clean—but if we put those same utensils in the basket, they come out perfect every time. Easy workaround, not a dealbreaker. Drying Performance Dishes come out dry, which already puts this unit ahead of many competitors. The only items that sometimes retain a bit of water are plastics or dishes with deep ridges that trap moisture. Plastic storage containers clean well and never melt, whether placed on the top or bottom rack. Compared to our twenty-year-old dishwasher, this is a night-and-day improvement. Noise Level This thing is whisper quiet. I can start it and sit about ten feet away watching TV without needing to raise the volume at all. Honestly, most of the time the only reason I know it's running is the red light projected onto the floor. Rack Design & Usability The third rack is fantastic for smaller items like travel mug lids and ramekins. Large baking sheets and big pots fit perfectly in the bottom rack. We do need to raise the top rack when loading oversized items, but the adjustable rack makes that simple and painless. Features That Matter The adjustable top rack is hands-down my favorite feature. Being able to lower it slightly to accommodate taller mugs is more useful than I expected. The app also turned out to be genuinely helpful. When we first installed the dishwasher, it wouldn't run a cycle. Using the app's troubleshooting tools, I was able to diagnose and fix the issue myself—no service call required. That alone was a win. Build Quality & Ease of Use The unit feels solid and well-built. Controls are intuitive and responsive with just a light touch. No complaints about usability or design. Reliability So Far We've only owned it a few months, but it has performed flawlessly. We've tested different cycles and drying modes, and everything has worked consistently without errors. Pros and Cons Biggest pro: The quiet operation. It's impressively silent. Biggest con: The app has a bit of a learning curve. Nothing is wrong with it—it just takes a little time to discover all of its features. Who It's For This dishwasher would be a great fit for almost any home. The only reason someone might hesitate is price—it's not the cheapest option out there. If you're on a very tight budget, it could be a stretch. But if you can afford it, the performance and quality absolutely justify the cost.

Sentence (English): We chose the Bosch SHP65CM5N because it felt like the best of both worlds: it fit within our budget while still offering many of the features we wanted in a modern dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Quiet, Powerful, worth the Investment ] || ---------------- || We chose the Bosch SHP65CM5N because it felt like the best of both worlds: it fit within our budget while still offering many of the features we wanted in a modern dishwasher. After several months of use, we'd rate it a solid 9 out of 10. I would absolutely buy it again and would confidently recommend it to others. Cleaning Performance. This dishwasher just works. Heavily soiled dishes and pans consistently come out sparkling clean on the first wash. We've had very few issues overall. The only minor exception is that occasionally heavily soiled utensils placed on the top rack don't get completely clean—but if we put those same utensils in the basket, they come out perfect every time. Easy workaround, not a dealbreaker. Drying Performance. Dishes come out dry, which already puts this unit ahead of many competitors. The only items that sometimes retain a bit of water are plastics or dishes with deep ridges that trap moisture. Plastic storage containers clean well and never melt, whether placed on the top or bottom rack. Compared to our twenty-year-old dishwasher, this is a night-and-day improvement. Noise Level. This thing is whisper quiet. I can start it and sit about ten feet away watching TV without needing to raise the volume at all. Honestly, most of the time the only reason I know it's running is the red light projected onto the floor. Rack Design & Usability. The third rack is fantastic for smaller items like travel mug lids and ramekins. Large baking sheets and big pots fit perfectly in the bottom rack. We do need to raise the top rack when loading oversized items, but the adjustable rack makes that simple and painless. Features That Matter. The adjustable top rack is hands-down my favorite feature. Being able to lower it slightly to accommodate taller mugs is more useful than I expected. The app also turned out to be genuinely helpful. When we first installed the dishwasher, it wouldn't run a cycle. Using the app's troubleshooting tools, I was able to diagnose and fix the issue myself—no service call required. That alone was a win. Build Quality & Ease of Use. The unit feels solid and well-built. Controls are intuitive and responsive with just a light touch. No complaints about usability or design. Reliability So Far. We've only owned it a few months, but it has performed flawlessly. We've tested different cycles and drying modes, and everything has worked consistently without errors. Pros and Cons. Sentence (English): I didn't expect a dishwasher to change my life… yet here we are.
Comments (English): [ 5 Star Bosch 300 Series Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I didn't expect a dishwasher to change my life… yet here we are. Suddenly, loading silverware feels organized and mature—like I've really got my life together now. And the drying? Let's just say my old dishwasher should be embarrassed. Bonus points for being energy efficient, whisper-quiet, and sleek enough to make my kitchen feel fancier than it probably deserves. I now find myself looking for excuses to run the dishwasher, which is a sentence I never thought I'd say. In summary: reliable, quiet, powerful, and oddly delightful. Five stars to Bosch for turning dish duty into a surprisingly satisfying experience. If this dishwasher were a person, I'd invite it to dinner—just so it could clean up afterward. Highly recommend. ️✨

Sentence (English): Overall it's good.
Comments (English): Overall it's good. I like small track on top for longer utensils. It has to be on the highest drying setting to get plastics to fully dry (which takes longer). And if you are looking for a fully recessed unit, this may not be right because the settings panel is on top and gets completely hidden when the door is closed unless it is mounted away from the cabinet (hence i can't see the status of the wash when it's running). Sentence (English): I installed it yesterday, and today I saw a 20,000 won discount.
Comments (English): I installed it yesterday, and today I saw a 20,000 won discount. My timing was just wrong. I installed it through Coupang, but the installer didn't seem to be a professional. It is slimmer than the basic 6-person model, so it seems to have a big advantage in homes with limited space, such as old houses or single-person homes.

Sentence (English): Purchasing appliances from Costco has been an absolute nightmare, and I strongly recommend that anyone reading this DON'T DO IT.
Comments (English): [ An absolute nightmare to deal with Costco ] || ---------------- || Purchasing appliances from Costco has been an absolute nightmare, and I strongly recommend that anyone reading this DON'T DO IT.I was originally scheduled to receive and have four kitchen appliances installed—a refrigerator, over-the-range microwave, range, and dishwasher—on Wednesday the 21st, between 9:30 AM and 11:30 AM. Two of these items were to be installed that same afternoon. I took a vacation day from work specifically to be home for this delivery and installation.Shortly before 10:00 AM, I received a call from Costco informing me that there was an issue with the truck and that my refrigerator and range would not be delivered that day. I was told that the installer would still arrive later with the microwave and dishwasher and complete the installation as scheduled. The delivery of the refrigerator and range was rescheduled for Saturday the 24th.Around 1:00 PM, the installer called and asked whether I had rescheduled my installation. I explained what Costco had told me and that I was still expecting him to arrive during his scheduled window of noon to 4:00 PM. However, 4:00 PM came and went with no installer and no communication.When I contacted the installer, he told me that my appointment had been removed from his schedule and that he no longer had my contact information. I then called Costco and was told that all four appliances would now be delivered and installed on the 24th.On the 25th, I received another call from Costco stating that the company responsible for installing the dishwasher and microwave only services my area on Wednesdays and Fridays. As a result, I was required to take yet another day off work for installation on the 28th.When the delivery team arrived on Saturday, they only brought two of the four appliances. I contacted Costco again and was told that the installer would bring the remaining appliances on the 28th, install them, and remove the old units.Now, on the 28th, I have been informed that the installer does not have the appliances and that installation must be rescheduled yet again, this time for February 4th.This ongoing lack of coordination, communication, and reliability is completely unacceptable. I have lost multiple workdays and have been repeatedly misled. At this point, all I want is a full refund.

Sentence (English): We just had this dishwasher installed by Certified Installs out of Salt Lake City as a part of the “Costco install”.
Comments (English): [ Installation was overly messy with hidden fees ] || ---------------- || We just had this dishwasher installed by Certified Installs out of Salt Lake City as a part of the “Costco install”. An old perfectly working dishwasher was being replaced because the door was starting to break. The installer said the drain pipe to our sink garbage disposal had to be replaced for an extra $134.56 in order for him to do the install. As the old one was being removed the installer used a glass jar to catch water. He broke the jar and tried to make it sound like it was our fault but that wasn't a big deal to us. As he was removing it on the dolly he dumped a lot of water on the floor and on multiple nice rugs which was annoying and avoidable. We had to clean it up because he wasn't equipped to deal with it and didn't seem interested in cleaning it up. That wasn't the less than professional part I was expecting and the drain pipe not being included was ridiculous. The positive is that we have a nice dishwasher installed that is super quiet. The installer did seem to do a good job overall and even pointed out some potential unrelated gutter problem if we didn't take action. He was just a bit lax in is guarding against issues he could have. The install is just a few hours old so there isn't much to say about the dishwasher. In the explanation of the dishwasher use the installer made is sound like the filter catch would have to be cleaned out every two weeks to two months.

Sentence (English): I figured how complex could a dishwasher be?
Comments (English): [ More than meets the eye ] || ---------------- || I figured how complex could a dishwasher be? Boy did I have a lot to learn (and still learning). To start with this thing is huge, not in actual size but the amount of dishes and cutlery it can hold. Where my previous dishwasher held maybe 4 or 5 meals worth of dishes the Bosch easily holds twice that amount, and with smart loading probably more. It's whisper quiet, if it weren't for the light that burns when it's running it would be easy to mistake it for not running. there are numerous cycles, and each one is customizable, want a light wash with sanitizer? easy. Need a full load with extra drying time? not a problem. I feel like I've barely scratched the surface when it comes to custom cycles. The wifi connection to the app running on a phone or tablet is amazing. It keeps me informed on what it's doing, and lets me know when a cycle is done. The app is always making suggestions on using the unit, it sends hints and tips on how to make better use of the product. while not the least expensive dishwasher on the market it epitomizes the statement you get what you pay for. And speaking of paying my water bill dropped since using the bosch 500, it's possible it will pay for itself over a long lifetime. Highly recommended

Comments (English): [ Disappointing machine ] || ---------------- || I'm sad to say that I do not recommend this Bosch dishwasher. We've now had this model for just over a year. We regretted not keeping the racks from our old machine (just in case they would fit) because they were perfect. The new racks create a lot of wasted space. Our big issue with this dishwasher is that it stopped consistently cleaning our dishes about 11 months in. There would be dish detergent residue in the basket and the silverware on top wasn't getting clean. The dishwasher was also making a faint straining noise. We followed some troubleshooting advice and made sure the sprayers were clean and nothing was impeding the dishwasher spray but we still had an issue. We called Bosch for warranty service and arranged for a local company to send a technician. The technician said everything was fine and then charged us $200. We were shocked at the charge, but he said that was Bosch policy. So we are out $200 and our dishwasher still doesn't clean our dishes. We resigned ourselves to having to live with this dishwasher with poor results. We removed the top silverware rack and had to put the basket in the bottom which further reduces the space in the machine. The dishwasher is still making a straining noise and sometimes we have to run dishes through run more than once or hand wash the items that don't get clean (and we don't overload the dishwasher or block the sprayers.) This is very frustrating for a $1300+ dishwasher. I am disappointed in Bosch costumer service as we have been happy with several other Bosch appliances over the years but we will be looking at another brand for our next dishwasher. This one was a waste of money.

Sentence (English): Last December, I moved and the last appliance I received was an LG dishwasher.
Comments (English): Last December, I moved and the last appliance I received was an LG dishwasher. I subscribed to maintenance services for filter management, sterilization, and installation, but the installer scraped the floor. I had it installed in the afternoon on the day of moving in, so I was so out of it that I couldn't check the problem right away when the installer was there. After the installer left, I found out about the floor problem. After the weekend, I contacted the customer service center, and they responded as if they were asking why I was only bringing it up now. Some footage of the work being done by the U+ Internet technicians overlapped with their visit times, and when I relayed this to the customer service center and other staff, they requested proof and even attached it, which only made the consumer feel like they were being treated worse. LG is currently denying responsibility for the floor scratches, saying that the home cam did not capture all of the technician's installation work. It clearly appears to be a scratch caused by the sink leg while moving the lower cabinet after removing it. There was another similar mark, but fortunately, it was not a dig and was wiped away. Regarding the floor scratches that I raised with LG, not only has there been no apology or compensation, but they are also denying responsibility based only on the attached photos and the home cam footage that the consumer sent without even confirming the site. As a consumer, I wonder if the work was done without carpeting or other maintenance work along the path where appliances and furniture were moved. I don't understand at all. The logistics center's excuse is that the carpet was lost by the technician when they came to my house, so they couldn't repair it. I'm really speechless. Every time I see the dishwasher, I get angry. Why did I sign a new contract when I left the old dishwasher behind? I'm so angry at myself. Also, after a long time, the customer service center contacted me regarding the payment method and my flooring complaint. I'm amazed at LG's ridiculous handling of the situation. I contacted the customer service center earlier this month to request a change to card payment, but they said the money had been debited from my account and that they would cancel the payment and reprocess it. When I checked the date of debit from my account, it was in the middle of this month. In other words, it seems that when I requested card payment at the customer service center, it wasn't processed and was withdrawn from my account. Regardless of the payment method, it's ironic that they're only contacting me now when I contacted the customer service center earlier this month. Comments (English): Last December, I moved and the last appliance I received was an LG dishwasher. I subscribed to maintenance services for filter management, sterilization, and installation, but the installer scraped the floor. I had it installed in the afternoon on the day of moving in, so I was so out of it that I couldn't check the problem right away when the installer was there. After the installer left, I found out about the floor problem. After the weekend, I contacted the customer service center, and they responded as if they were asking why I was only bringing it up now. Some footage of the work being done by the U+ Internet technicians overlapped with their visit times, and when I relayed this to the customer service center and other staff, they requested proof and even attached it, which only made the consumer feel like they were being treated worse. LG is currently denying responsibility for the floor scratches, saying that the home cam did not capture all of the technician's installation work. It clearly appears to be a scratch caused by the sink leg while moving the lower cabinet after removing it. There was another similar mark, but fortunately, it was not a dig and was wiped away. Regarding the floor scratches that I raised with LG, not only has there been no apology or compensation, but they are also denying responsibility based only on the attached photos and the home cam footage that the consumer sent without even confirming the site. Regardless of the payment method, it's ironic that they're only contacting me now when I contacted the customer service center earlier this month. Sentence (English): After the installer left, I found out about the floor problem.
Comments (English): Last December, I moved and the last appliance I received was an LG dishwasher. I subscribed to maintenance services for filter management, sterilization, and installation, but the installer scraped the floor. I had it installed in the afternoon on the day of moving in, so I was so out of it that I couldn't check the problem right away when the installer was there. After the installer left, I found out about the floor problem. After the weekend, I contacted the customer service center, and they responded as if they were asking why I was only bringing it up now. Some footage of the work being done by the U+ Internet technicians overlapped with their visit times, and when I relayed this to the customer service center and other staff, they requested proof and even attached it, which only made the consumer feel like they were being treated worse. LG is currently denying responsibility for the floor scratches, saying that the home cam did not capture all of the technician's installation work. It clearly appears to be a scratch caused by the sink leg while moving the lower cabinet after removing it. There was another similar mark, but fortunately, it was not a dig and was wiped away. Regarding the floor scratches that I raised with LG, not only has there been no apology or compensation, but they are also denying responsibility based only on the attached photos and the home cam footage that the consumer sent without even confirming the site. The logistics center's excuse is that the carpet was lost by the technician when they came to my house, so they couldn't repair it. I'm really speechless. Every time I see the dishwasher, I get angry. Why did I sign a new contract when I left the old dishwasher behind? I'm so angry at myself. In other words, it seems that when I requested card payment at the customer service center, it wasn't processed and was withdrawn from my account. Regardless of the payment method, it's ironic that they're only contacting me now when I contacted the customer service center earlier this month. Comments (English): Last December, I moved and the last appliance I received was an LG dishwasher. I had it installed in the afternoon on the day of moving in, so I was so out of it that I couldn't check the problem right away when the installer was there. Sentence (English): I'm amazed at LG's ridiculous handling of the situation.
Comments (English): Last December, I moved and the last appliance I received was an LG dishwasher. I subscribed to maintenance services for filter management, sterilization, and installation, but the installer scraped the floor. I had it installed in the afternoon on the day of moving in, so I was so out of it that I couldn't check the problem right away when the installer was there. After the installer left, I found out about the floor problem. After the weekend, I contacted the customer service center, and they responded as if they were asking why I was only bringing it up now. Some footage of the work being done by the U+ Internet technicians overlapped with their visit times, and when I relayed this to the customer service center and other staff, they requested proof and even attached it, which only made the consumer feel like they were being treated worse. LG is currently denying responsibility for the floor scratches, saying that the home cam did not capture all of the technician's installation work. It clearly appears to be a scratch caused by the sink leg while moving the lower cabinet after removing it. There was another similar mark, but fortunately, it was not a dig and was wiped away. Regarding the floor scratches that I raised with LG, not only has there been no apology or compensation, but they are also denying responsibility based only on the attached photos and the home cam footage that the consumer sent without even confirming the site. As a consumer, I wonder if the work was done without carpeting or other maintenance work along the path where appliances and furniture were moved. I don't understand at all. The logistics center's excuse is that the carpet was lost by the technician when they came to my house, so they couldn't repair it. I'm really speechless. Every time I see the dishwasher, I get angry. Why did I sign a new contract when I left the old dishwasher behind? I'm so angry at myself. Also, after a long time, the customer service center contacted me regarding the payment method and my flooring complaint. I'm amazed at LG's ridiculous handling of the situation. I contacted the customer service center earlier this month to request a change to card payment, but they said the money had been debited from my account and that they would cancel the payment and reprocess it. When I checked the date of debit from my account, it was in the middle of this month. In other words, it seems that when I requested card payment at the customer service center, it wasn't processed and was withdrawn from my account. Regardless of the payment method, it's ironic that they're only contacting me now when I contacted the customer service center earlier this month. Even though I said I would look into the Maru complaint issue again and get back to you during a phone call last Thursday regarding payment, I haven't heard back yet, so it seems like they are making fun of consumers. The more I think about it, the more I realize how great LG Electronics' response capabilities are.

Comments (English): Last December, I moved and the last appliance I received was an LG dishwasher. I had it installed in the afternoon on the day of moving in, so I was so out of it that I couldn't check the problem right away when the installer was there. After the installer left, I found out about the floor problem. After the weekend, I contacted the customer service center, and they responded as if they were asking why I was only bringing it up now. Some footage of the work being done by the U+ Internet technicians overlapped with their visit times, and when I relayed this to the customer service center and other staff, they requested proof and even attached it, which only made the consumer feel like they were being treated worse. LG is currently denying responsibility for the floor scratches, saying that the home cam did not capture all of the technician's installation work. It clearly appears to be a scratch caused by the sink leg while moving the lower cabinet after removing it. There was another similar mark, but fortunately, it was not a dig and was wiped away. Regarding the floor scratches that I raised with LG, not only has there been no apology or compensation, but they are also denying responsibility based only on the attached photos and the home cam footage that the consumer sent without even confirming the site. Sentence (English): Hello, I'm a mom of two sons, ages 6 and 8 months.
Comments (English): Hello, I'm a mom of two sons, ages 6 and 8 months. I order from Coupang once a month, but I don't have time to write reviews. Still, I'm happy with the products I'm writing, so I hope it's helpful to others. I hope this review helps. I didn't buy a dishwasher because I heard it only runs for an hour or two. I could just do it quickly, so I thought, why waste so much energy on washing? Oh, robot vacuum. After trying the robot vacuum, I changed my mind and decided to install it. My kitchen is old, so it's quite small. The installation costs are high, and I didn't think I'd have enough space, so I hesitated for a while. I bought it in advance and asked the installer if it would be possible. He said yes, and I did. The installation took about two hours, and after it was finished, he came right away to install it. Wow. The installation only cost 100,000 won. Of course, it depends on the space, but I'm so satisfied because it was so much less than I expected. In fact, I was worried a lot because there wasn't much difference between a 14-person Ku* dishwasher and one with a steam function, but I saw in reviews that Ku* often gets hit in the back with long-term installation costs, so I chose LG, which I trust, and I'm very satisfied. Now, I don't have to worry about washing dishes in the evening, so I can put them in and play with the kids. It's cleaner because there are no dirty dishes on the sink, especially. Seeing the glass is sparkling clean makes me feel like I made a great purchase. Recommended! Coupang is the cheapest. They deliver quickly, so it's advantageous to use it more often. Oh, and ours is a 12-person one, but it's perfect for a family of four. We cook a lot of pots and pans. Dinner is full in one sitting. I'm glad I didn't buy the 14-person one. It's enough.

Sentence (English): I am very pleased with the performance of this dishwasher so far.
Comments (English): [ Very practicle dishwasher with appropiate cycles ] || ---------------- || I am very pleased with the performance of this dishwasher so far. The lower rack accommodates the tallest of plates, pots and pans like no other dishwasher I have owned before. A very convenient feature is that all of the plate supports on the lower rack fold down giving a totally flat area for loading several large pots, bowls and pans at the same time. All of the upper rack plate supports fold down too allowing more space for larger items that perhaps didn't fit in the lower rack. The height adjustable foldable flaps on each side of the upper rack can be folded down to accomadate lager utensils. The slots work well with tall stemmed glasses too. The easily height adjustable upper rack is great for optimising the space below or above it. The cutlery rack is very spacious with a deep central trough to accommodate larger items. I particularly like the Rapid Program which will do a complete wash, rinse and dry cycle in about 33 minutes for when my dishes need "shining" rather than a thorough wash. Another great feature is the Extra Dry option which can be added to the end of most cycles for a more dry result, as there remains slight dampness on the items after the completion of the cycle. My previous dishwahers were the same in this respect. This dishwasher has a Natural Dry function which will open the door slightly at the end of the cycle to help with the drying process. This function can be deactivated if you don't like it as steam does rise up into the kitchen furniture. Rinse aid must be used otherwise the dishwasher drips heavily with water at the end of its cycle. Another feature I like is the large LED display is white rather than red as other brands often use. There is one feature that was on my previous machine but is ommitted on this Whirlpool dishwasher. That is, it does not memorize the last cycle used, so that after turning on the machine each time the cycle has to be individually selected. Not really a big inconvenience but, having to press only two buttons, ON followed by START would be my preference as I mostly use the same cycle each time. The unusually long manufacturer's warranty of 5 years gave me the confidence when purchasing this dishwasher. Compared with other big brand dishwashers that are often more expensive this Whirlpool dishwasher is well featured and has so far met with my expectations. I am looking forward to this machine fulfilling its fuction beyond its warranty period.

This releases steam into the kitchen but allows the dishes to dry passively. I REALLY like this appliance. It is well designed and of top-quality construction. I appreciate its network connectivity and smartphone integration, but these can be ignored by old schoolers who just want button control and local monitoring via the door top panel.

I've been using the Bosch 300 Series dishwasher for about a month, and I'm very happy with how it performs. Right from the start, it's consistently delivered excellent cleaning results, even when dishes are loaded straight after meals with only a quick scrape. The PrecisionWash sensors do an impressive job, and I've found that plates and glassware come out spotless every time without the need for pre-rinsing. One of the features I appreciate most is how quiet it runs. I can operate it during meals or while working nearby and barely notice it's on. It definitely lives up to its reputation for low-noise performance at 46 dBA. The third rack is another big plus, especially for utensils and smaller items. It creates more room on the lower racks and makes loading much more efficient. I also find the RackMatic adjustable racks very useful when I need extra space for taller cookware or stemware. Drying performance is solid for dishes and metal items. That said, like many models without a built-in heating element, plastic containers can sometimes remain slightly wet and may need a quick wipe or extra air-drying time. The stainless-steel interior feels durable and is easy to maintain, and the AquaStop Plus leak protection adds reassurance against potential water damage. The Home Connect Wi-Fi features are a convenient extra, allowing me to monitor cycles or start a wash remotely from my phone. Overall, I'd strongly recommend this dishwasher to anyone looking for a dependable, quiet, and efficient appliance for everyday use. While plastic drying could be a bit better, it's a minor drawback compared to how well everything else works.

Sentence (English): I recently purchased/upgraded to the LDFN4542S, and I couldn't be happier with the decision.
Comments (English): [ Excellent Performance and a Fresh Start with LG ] || ---------------- || I recently purchased/upgraded to the LDFN4542S, and I couldn't be happier with the decision. This dishwasher is truly excellent, providing top-tier cleaning and drying performance. While some people might be surprised I stuck with the same brand after my last experience, the truth is that I was always very happy with the actual washing and drying results of my previous LG. Because the cleaning performance was so reliable when the machine was running, I decided to give their newer generation a fair shot.My previous unit was the LDT5678ST, which was a bit of a saga as that model was actually part of a class-action lawsuit. I had the control board fail within the first year, which the warranty covered, but the issues didn't stop there. the following year LG offered their extended warranty via email, so I purchased an extended LG warranty, and only six months after that, the board began failing yet again. However, because this happened during the pandemic when parts were incredibly scarce, LG ended up paying me out for the full cost of the dishwasher.Because of that payout, the dishwasher was essentially free for the duration I owned it. I managed to keep it limping along for another three years after the settlement, getting a total of seven years out of the machine. Recently, the motor started squealing loudly, so I figured it was finally time to retire it and get a new one.This new LDFN4542S takes everything I liked about the cleaning power of my old one and seems to have refined it. It is worth noting that this model does not have Wi-Fi capabilities, which in my opinion are useless anyway; I never used them on my old unit, so I don't miss them at all. The washing is great, and the drying performance is even better than I expected. It's quiet, efficient, and handles tough messes with ease. After the long journey with my last machine, I'm optimistic that this one will provide the same great results with better long-term reliability.To play it safe, I also made sure to get the 5-year Geek Squad warranty with this purchase. That is another big positive point for me, as I've had great experiences with their service in the past. If you want a dishwasher that actually gets your dishes clean and dry the first time, this is a great choice.

Sentence (English): Really happy with the performance of the Bosch Benchmarck dishwasher.

We have hard water and with the water softening feature we have seen a noticable difference in the cleanliness of the glassware. Also like the internal light contained int the unit. I was surprised to see the Bosch Benchmark had a projected time and cycle indicator that could be reflected onto the floor. My only suggestion for improvement would be the hose connection, Would have preferred a brass fitting instead of the nylon connector.

Comments (English): [ Good but in need of improvement ] || ---------------- || I am a builder and property owner. I recently pulled the LG DW from a house that will undergo a gut renovation and installed the LG unit in my own home. At the time of removal the DW was, and still is in excellent cosmetic condition and all the controls are working properly. Two issues we have encountered are as follows:1: the bottom rotating spray assembly is so close to the lower rack that if an item sticks out below the rack as little as 3/16” the spray assembly will hit the item. This is not nearly enough clearance and coupled with the rather wide spacing of the lower rack bars, we need to be extremely vigilant. 2: On occasion the detergent pod (we use a Kirkland brand pod) does not release from the detergent tray. The trap door opens, the pod gets wet and the outer coating starts to dissolve but for reasons I don't understand it does not drop out and down. Seems like it's not getting enough water for a long enough duration to ensure it gets flushed out of the dispenser tray. Cleaning quality in general has been quite good (unless one of the two issues mentioned above is at play)The unit is extremely quit. The exterior handle looks good, but it is a crumb catcher. The top, silverware tray has been a nice upgrade from our prior Bosch unit, but on a few occasions some of the flatware did not get completely clean. I am aware this model has been discontinued, so I can't speak to any improvements that LG has made. Bottom line, I don't think it is as good as the Bosch at the same price point. I hope you find my comments to be informative. Good luck.

Sentence (English): I am a builder and property owner.
Comments (English): [ Good but in need of improvement ] || ---------------- || I am a builder and property owner. I recently pulled the LG DW from a house that will undergo a gut renovation and installed the LG unit in my own home. At the time of removal the DW was, and still is in excellent cosmetic condition and all the controls are working properly. Two issues we have encountered are as follows:1: the bottom rotating spray assembly is so close to the lower rack that if an item sticks out below the rack as little as 1/4" the spray assembly will hit the item. This is not nearly enough clearance and coupled with the rather wide spacing of the lower rack bars, we need to be extremely vigilant. 2: On occasion the detergent pod (we use a Kirkland brand pod) does not release from the detergent tray. The trap door opens, the pod gets wet and the outer coating starts to dissolve but for reasons I don't understand it does not drop out and down. Seems like it's not getting enough water for a long enough duration to ensure it gets flushed out of the dispenser tray. Cleaning quality in general has been quite good (unless one of the two issues mentioned above is at play)The unit is extremely quit. The exterior handle looks good, but it is a crumb catcher. The top, silverware tray has been a nice upgrade from our prior Bosch unit, but on a few occasions some of the flatware did not get completely clean. I am aware this model has been discontinued, so I can't speak to any improvements that LG has made. Bottom line, I don't think it is as good as the Bosch at the same price point. I hope you find my comments to be informative. Good luck.

Sentence (English): I am a builder and property owner.
Comments (English): [ Good but in need of improvement ] || ---------------- || I am a builder and property owner. I recently pulled the LG DW from a house that will undergo a gut renovation and installed the LG unit in my own home. At the time of removal the DW was, and still is in excellent cosmetic condition and all the controls are working properly. Two issues we have encountered are as follows:1: the bottom rotating spray assembly is so close to the lower rack that if an item sticks out below the rack as little as 1/4” the spray assembly will hit the item. This is not nearly enough clearance and coupled with the rather wide spacing of the lower rack bars, we need to be extremely vigilant. 2: On occasion the detergent pod (we use a Kirkland brand pod) does not release from the detergent tray. The trap door opens, the pod gets wet and the outer coating starts to dissolve but for reasons I don't understand it does not drop out and down. Seems like it's not getting enough water for a long enough duration to ensure it gets flushed out of the dispenser tray. Cleaning quality in general has been quite good (unless one of the two issues mentioned above is at play)The unit is extremely quit. The exterior handle looks good, but it is a crumb catcher. The top, silverware tray has been a nice upgrade from our prior Bosch unit, but on a few occasions some of the flatware did not get completely clean. I am aware this model has been discontinued, so I can't speak to any improvements that LG has made. Bottom line, I don't think it is as good as the Bosch at the same price point. I hope you find my comments to be informative. Good luck.

Sentence (English): We really like our Bosch dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Near perfection, but not quite ] || ---------------- || We really like our Bosch dishwasher. It's as quiet as promised, which is much appreciated by those who have had noisy dishwashers (like us ;>). And it does a great job of cleaning our dishes. Two primary suggestions: surely Bosch can figure out a way to dry the dishes better. This isn't a big deal - we were advised of it before purchase - but there's room for improvement. However, the main thing for us is that all the tines in the bottom rack are pointed at an angle, which makes it difficult to place larger items. Your dishwashers should have a number of tines that point straight up - then it would be close to perfect. An additional thing is the lack of a user interface for selecting extended dry or sanitize. The instructions for doing so are quite, um. lame. I've installed the app on my phone, so it's not a problem for us, but I can imagine an older person really struggling to understand the user manual instructions. So there you go. Thanks for all the fine engineering that you folks build into your products.

Comments (English): [ Noisy Kitchenaid KDFS424SPS ] || ---------------- || We bought this unit on 1/14/26 and it was delivered 1/17/26. We ran a couple of settings to determine if this would make a difference and it did not. We really wanted to love this unit as the controls are simple, it's very well laid out inside, love the 3 racks, and the cleaning and drying are fantastic (love the pop-open door feature after it's finished). We had a 14 year old lower-end Bosch that died and it was very quiet. Unfortunately we are returning this unit and will replace with a Bosch.

Sentence (English): We purchased the Bosch Super Silent Plus 38 dBA dishwasher expecting premium performance commensurate with the price and reputation.
Comments (English): [ Super Quiet but VERY poor Drying Performance ] || ---------------- || We purchased the Bosch Super Silent Plus 38 dBA dishwasher expecting premium performance commensurate with the price and reputation. While it is impressively quiet and cleans dishes well, the drying performance has been extremely disappointing. After running a full cycle and leaving the dishwasher unopened, we returned two days later to find the interior still very damp, with visible moisture throughout. We understand Bosch uses condensation drying, but this level of retained moisture feels excessive and raises concerns about hygiene, odor, and mold — especially for households that travel or don't unload immediately. We used rinse aid, proper loading, and appropriate cycles, yet the results did not improve. For a high-end appliance, we expected better drying outcomes or at least clearer communication that dishes and the interior may remain wet long after a cycle finishes. This may be acceptable to some users, but for us, the trade-off between silence and basic drying performance is not worth it. We're disappointed, as we wanted to love this dishwasher, but it doesn't meet our expectations for daily usability or peace of mind.
